stubs.service: Anthropic Messages API (article summaries, translation, AI chat with tool use, chat title generation)
stubs.how: .ui-capture/stub/stub.mjs listens on 127.0.0.1:4536 (PORT+101) and implements POST /v1/messages (JSON and SSE streaming, incl. tool_use blocks). The server's @anthropic-ai/sdk client is pointed at it with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL; settings hold a placeholder api_key.anthropic. Summaries are built from the article's own sentences/headings; home-screen chat first calls the app's real search_articles tool, then answers with links to the returned articles; article chat answers from the article text in the system prompt.

.ui-capture/stub/stub.mjs also starts an in-memory Meilisearch-compatible HTTP API (.ui-capture/stub/meili-stub.mjs) on 127.0.0.1:4537 (PORT+102, MEILI_URL). It covers index create/delete/swap/stats, settings, document add/update/delete, tasks and search with filters/sort. The server rebuilds the index into it on every startup. The real meilisearch binary can't run in this sandbox: its LMDB memory-map sizing fails with EPERM.

stubs.service: Google favicon service (https://www.google.com/s2/favicons, loaded directly by the browser)
stubs.how: After `vite build`, .ui-capture/build.sh rewrites that URL in dist/assets/*.js to /__stub/favicons. The gateway in stub.mjs (the process listening on PORT 4435, which proxies everything else to the Fastify server on 4535) answers it with a colored letter-icon SVG for each domain.
Seeded og_image values point to /__stub/og/<slug>.svg, which the gateway renders as gradient cover images, so no remote image CDN is contacted.

stubs.service: RSS feed fetching (outbound HTTP to feed sites)
stubs.how: Not called: CRON_SCHEDULE is set to once a year so the 5-minute fetch cron never runs offline. Feeds/articles come from the seed instead.

Bypassed with the app's own local sign-in bypass: start.sh runs the server with AUTH_DISABLED=1 (which the server only accepts together with NODE_ENV=development) and NO_SEED=1, so /api/me answers {"email":"local"} and the UI opens signed in. The seeded password account (maya.lindqvist@fastmail.com / fjellstue-2026) still exists in the DB but isn't needed.

app.notes: Oksskolten runs through its own Fastify server (NODE_ENV=development + AUTH_DISABLED=1, the app's built-in local sign-in bypass, so the UI opens already signed in; NO_SEED=1 skips the repo demo seed) (server/index.ts via tsx), serving the Vite build in ./dist, with SQLite (libsql) at .ui-capture/data/rss.db. Setup: mise.toml pins node 22.23.5 + npm 11.12.1 (+ conftest from the repo). .ui-capture/build.sh runs npm ci, vite build and the favicon rewrite. .ui-capture/start.sh re-seeds the DB on every start (so relative dates stay fresh), then starts stub.mjs (gateway :4435, Anthropic :4536, Meilisearch :4537) and the server (:4535). Seed (.ui-capture/seed/seed.ts, using the app's migrations and schema) creates the user's account, settings (English, Anthropic provider, thumbnails on) and the dataset: the repo's own demo feeds/articles/chat conversations (src/lib/demo/seed) plus a generated extension (.ui-capture/seed/extra.ts, feeds-extra.ts, text-pools.ts). Result: 10 categories (Languages, Infrastructure, Platform, Databases, Web & Frontend, AI & ML, Security, Engineering Culture, News [collapsed], 日本語) plus uncategorized feeds; 38 feeds (Clips included), among them an RSS-Bridge feed, a JS-challenge feed, LWN failing with HTTP 403 (6 errors) and a disabled dead feed (ENOTFOUND); ~250 articles published over ~7 months, most in the last 2 months: ~80 unread, ~120 read, ~25 bookmarked, ~18 liked, ~90 with AI summaries, cover images on ~2/3, 7 failed extractions with no full text, Japanese articles (read ones carry English translations), 5 hand-clipped pages; 8 chat conversations (3 from the repo demo); similar-article links. Main areas: Inbox/Home article list (list/card/magazine layouts), feed sidebar grouped by category with unread counts and feed error states, article reader with AI summary and chat, Bookmarks, Likes, History, Chat page with past conversations, search (Cmd+K), Settings (appearance themes, reading, AI providers, feeds/OPML, security, retention). The entry page / opens straight into the signed-in Home/Inbox view.

This is a checkout of babarot/oksskolten (https://github.com/babarot/oksskolten) at commit 737526230a9c. 🏔️ The AI-native RSS reader

I want to see its user interface in a desktop browser, in the state a real, established user would see it. Please get the app running locally with its main interface working and realistic data in it.

# Running it
- Follow the repo's own setup docs and tooling. Take the simplest route that shows the real app: a static production build if the front end works without a backend, otherwise the app's own server (production or dev mode).
- If it needs a database or other services, run them locally with an embedded or file-based option (SQLite, in-memory, JSON files, an embedded Postgres such as PGlite) or the app's demo/mock mode.
- Don't redesign or restyle anything. Change only what's needed to build and run it.

# Tools: use mise
Install every runtime and tool you need (node, the package manager, python, bun, ...) with mise, pinned to exact versions in a mise.toml at the repo root, so the setup can be reproduced. Match what the repo asks for (engines, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, packageManager). mise is already configured for this directory: `mise install` installs into ./.ui-capture/mise, and its shims come first on PATH, so `node`, `pnpm` and the rest resolve to the pinned versions. Don't use other copies of these tools or download runtimes by hand.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. Wherever it expects secrets, environment variables, API keys or third-party services (hosted auth or OAuth, payment providers, email, LLM or other AI APIs, maps, storage buckets, analytics, hosted databases):
- Give the required variables placeholder values so the app starts.
- Where it actually calls the service, make the call succeed locally with realistic responses: use the app's own mock, test or offline mode if it has one; otherwise point the client at a small local stub server that start.sh also starts, or swap in a stub at the integration boundary (the API client or service module). Keep stubs out of UI code. Responses should look like what the real service returns for a real user, e.g. an AI reply that actually answers, a payment history with real-looking amounts.
- Calls the browser makes directly to outside services count too; point them at the local stub.
- For sign-in through an outside provider, create a local account or use the app's dev sign-in so you can get past it.
List every stub in app.json.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. No lorem ipsum or "Test 1".

# Environment
This shell is sandboxed: you can write only inside this directory (package-manager caches already point into ./.ui-capture/cache), and the network reaches only package registries, mise's download sources and GitHub (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, repo.yarnpkg.com, github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, nodejs.org, mise.jdx.dev, mise-versions.jdx.dev, release-assets.githubusercontent.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, binaries.prisma.sh, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com). Docker isn't available. A process you start in the background can't be seen or stopped from a later command, so test servers on another port than 4435 (e.g. 5435) or in the foreground under `timeout`; anything still listening on 4435 is stopped before I check.

# When you're done, leave this in ./.ui-capture/
- app.json: {"mode": "static" or "server", "entry": "/path where the main UI opens", "login": null or {"username": "...", "email": "...", "password": "..."}, "stubs": [{"service": "what was faked", "how": "how"}], "notes": "how you set it up, what data is loaded, and the main areas of the app"}
- static mode: the production build in ./.ui-capture/out, with index.html as its entry. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server; unknown paths fall back to index.html.
- server mode: ./.ui-capture/start.sh, which starts everything the app needs (stubs included) in the foreground and serves the UI at http://localhost:4435/ (it gets PORT=4435). It runs with the same PATH and restrictions as your shell, plus no network at all except localhost, so everything must already be installed, built and seeded (or seeded by start.sh itself).
- Put any scripts you write for seeding or stubbing in ./.ui-capture/ too; they're kept with the setup record.

# Order of work
You have 90 minutes in total, and anything unfinished when time runs out is lost. So work in this order:
1. Get the app building and running with its stubs, and write the contract above (app.json plus out/ or start.sh), even if it has only a little data so far.
2. Then build out the data, re-running your seed and checking the app still loads after each substantial step, so that a working state with the data loaded so far is always in place.
Write large data sets with a short generator script rather than as one long literal file.
